newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China overfly rights to boost Canadian cargo.
newsitem.headline: China overfly rights to boost Canadian cargo.

text.p: Canadian Airlines International Limited (CAI) says it will be able to fly more trans-Pacific cargo because of new overfly rights over China.
Tony Buckley, CAI's regional director for Asia said the new, shorter routing will cut around 40 minutes flying time on the Hong Kong-Vancouver service.
Other CAI Asian trans-Pacific services including Bangkok, Kuala Lumpur, Taipei and Manila will also have their flight times reduced, he said.
"It will be of great benefit to us and help us considerably in our operations. Any time you can cut off the flight means more passengers and more cargo can be carried," Buckley told Reuters.
He said the old, longer routing sometimes forced cargo weight restrictions on CAI's daily Boeing 747-400 flights between Hong Kong and Vancouver.
"Any overfly rights help us a lot especially between now and March when we face strong headwinds," he added. --Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax +44 171 542 5017
